Business justification: Strategic investment — model supply chain security is core to RHOAI trust strategy. The 'sign on store' capability was already delivered via STRAT-101; without 'verify on serve', that investment doesn't deliver its intended runtime integrity value. Customers in regulated industries are demanding end-to-end verifiable model provenance. This is also a competitive differentiator in the enterprise AI platform market, with upstream Sigstore ecosystem projects (ImagePolicy controller, Model Validation operator) providing building blocks.
User problem: Users who carefully sign AI models during storage have no assurance that the model actually being served matches what they signed. Admins have no guidance on how to set up Red Hat Trusted Artifact Signer with OpenShift AI to ensure model signatures are verified for deployed inference workloads. Signatures are completely ignored at serving time, making the existing signing workflow incomplete for runtime integrity guarantees.
Scope: Single focused need — signature verification enforcement at model serving time. Covers two model source formats: (1) models stored in S3/HuggingFace with model.sig (OpenSSF Model Signature), and (2) OCI ModelCar images with Cosign signatures and embedded OpenSSF Model Signatures. Verification must integrate with KServe and llm-d serving infrastructure. Policy flexibility needed (hard-stop vs. warning-only).
Success criteria: Admins can configure signature verification policies for model serving. Models from S3/HuggingFace with model.sig are verified before serving. OCI ModelCar images are verified (container image signature and/or embedded OpenSSF Model Signature) before serving. Clear pass/fail feedback is provided to both admins and users when verification fails. Policy-driven enforcement allows admins to choose between blocking deployment or issuing warnings. The end-to-end story — sign on store, verify on serve — provides a complete trust chain for AI model provenance.", "priority": "Critical", "prompt": "We already invested in model signing at storage time through AI Hub and Trusted Artifact Signer, but there's no verification happening when those models are actually served via KServe or llm-d. **WHAT (2/2):** The RFE clearly articulates what is needed — model signature verification at serving time for KServe/llm-d, covering OpenSSF Model Signatures for S3/HuggingFace models and Cosign signatures for OCI ModelCar images, with policy-driven enforcement (hard-stop vs. audit mode). This is specific and well-defined.

**WHY (2/2):** Strong business justification with named customer segments (FSI, government, regulated industries), explicit mention of it being a "blocker for deals in regulated-AI segment," strategic completion of the STRAT-101 supply-chain security investment, and competitive positioning rationale.

**Open to HOW (2/2):** The RFE describes customer-facing outcomes (config UI, feedback, audit logs) without mandating specific implementation details. Engineering retains freedom on architecture (admission webhook vs. controller, policy storage model, etc.).

**Not a task (2/2):** This is clearly a business-driven feature need addressing a security gap for regulated customers, not housekeeping or a technical chore.

**Right-sized (2/2):** Single coherent feature — model signature verification with policy enforcement. The multiple acceptance criteria (S3 verification, OCI Cosign, embedded signatures, feedback, audit logging) all serve the same unified need.

The review also provides excellent feasibility analysis and strategy considerations, flagging appropriate items for the strategy phase (policy storage model, multi-path verification logic, FIPS alignment, architectural boundaries, rollout phasing, audit logging integration) while correctly noting no blockers.

The `needs_attention: true` flag with a clear reason is appropriate — it correctly identifies that while the RFE itself is well-written, strategy phase needs to resolve several architectural questions.

**Verdict:** The pipeline correctly identified a high-quality RFE (perfect 10/10 score) and appropriately decided not to revise it.
